title: Which of the last three claims about values are right?
description: Three claims about expressions with two letters are checked by putting in both numbers, multiplying first, and working out any bracket. Keeko doubts the first check and takes away the numbers before multiplying.
teaching_notes: One idea: put in both numbers, work out the bracket, multiply, and only then add or take away. Watch for students who subtract the two numbers before they multiply.

source: Check these claims. 7: if f = 3 and g = 1, then 2f − 2g = 2. 8: if t = 4 and b = 3, then 2t + b = 24. 9: if h = 5 and n = 6, then h − (3 − n) = 4.
video_script.why: A learner sees that a claim with two letters is checked by putting in both numbers and working in the right order: bracket, multiplication, then adding or taking away.
video_script.substitution: The book's own three claims, checked one by one.
video_script.anchor: three claims, each with two letters, their numbers, and a stated value
video_script.wrong_answer: two f minus two g is two times two
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko works out 3 − 1 = 2 first and then multiplies by 2, but multiplication comes first: 2 × 3 − 2 × 1 = 6 − 2 = 4.
video_script.payoff_line: None of the three claims is right

final_answer.spoken: the true values are four, eleven and eight, so none of the three claims is right

never_show: the three true values together before the answer beat
video_script.design: One idea: put in both numbers and work in the right order. Assumes the value of an expression for a given number. The three claims stay on the stage and each is crossed out when it fails. Wrong idea: take away the numbers before multiplying.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; three cards, each holding a claim about an expression with two letters and their numbers

marks.p1: the title card From your book arrives
marks.p2: three new cards appear, each with a claim
marks.p3: the two letters, their numbers and the stated value are highlighted on each card
marks.p4: a question mark glows over the three cards

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>It gives the last three claims about the values of expressions.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>Each claim names two letters, the numbers they stand for, and a value.
<bookmark mark='p4'/>Which of these claims are right?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a claim card; two number tiles slide into the slots of two letters; a ladder with brackets, then multiplication, then adding or taking away

marks.g1: two number tiles slide into the slots where the letters sit
marks.g2: a ladder appears with brackets first, multiplication next, and adding or taking away last
marks.g3: the true value and the stated value are placed side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>To check a claim, we put each number in place of its letter.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Then we follow the order: brackets first, then multiplication, then adding or taking away.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>We compare the true value with the stated value.

beats.on_screen: Given: 7: if f = 3 and g = 1, then 2f − 2g = 2 ; 8: if t = 4 and b = 3, then 2t + b = 24 ; 9: if h = 5 and n = 6, then h − (3 − n) = 4

marks.gv2: the eighth claim is written under it
marks.gv3: the ninth claim is written under that

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, the seventh claim says two f minus two g is two. Here f is three and g is one.
<bookmark mark='gv2'/>The eighth says two t plus b is twenty four. Here t is four and b is three.
<bookmark mark='gv3'/>The ninth says h minus the bracket three minus n is four. Here h is five and n is six.

beats.on_screen: To find: the true value in each claim, and whether the claim is right
narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We find the true value in each claim, and see if the claim is right.

marks.s1a: 3 is put in place of f and 1 in place of g

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>For the seventh claim, put three for f and one for g.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Both multiplications come first, giving six and two.
<bookmark mark='s1c'/>Six minus two is four, so the seventh claim is not right.

marks.s2a: 4 is put in place of t and 3 in place of b

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>For the eighth claim, put four for t and three for b.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Two times four is eight, and eight plus three is eleven. The eighth claim is not right.

marks.s3a: 5 is put in place of h and 6 in place of n

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>For the ninth claim, put five for h and six for n.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>The bracket is worked first, and three minus six is minus three.
<bookmark mark='s3c'/>Taking away minus three adds three, so the value is five plus three, which is eight. The ninth claim is not right.

marks.ans: all three claims are crossed out
marks.ans2: the three true values are boxed together

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>None of the three claims is right.
<bookmark mark='ans2'/>The true values are four, eleven and eight.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

marks.d2: the numbers 3 and 1 are circled and joined by a minus sign
marks.d3: the bubble is struck out and the two multiplications are written beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Keeko thinks two f minus two g is two times two, because three minus one is two.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>That takes away the numbers first, before the multiplications are done.
<bookmark mark='d3'/>But multiplication comes first, so the products are six and two. Six minus two is four.
